sections.overview: This dwarf cichlid was described from the Río Pintuyacu in Peru’s Loreto region. Later records extend its known range to nearby Nanay and southern Tapiche drainages.
sections.identification: The type series’ adult male measured 34.4 mm standard length; adult females measured 26.1–28.2 mm, measured to the tail-fin base. Males have extended front dorsal lobes and tail rays; both sexes show the unique lower tail-stalk blotch and narrow side stripe.
sections.habitat: It inhabits slow tributaries, creeks and backwaters with soft, acidic clear or black water and fallen leaf litter on the bottom.
sections.diet: A species-specific prey list has not been documented; genus-level accounts describe Apistogramma as carnivorous, mainly taking small bottom-dwelling invertebrates.
sections.behavior: Captive observations describe territorial males that may attack rival males. Some pairs reportedly settle better when other conspecific pairs remain visible nearby.
sections.reproduction: Captive reports describe cave spawning at night or dawn, usually with 50–150 eggs. The male patrols while the female guards and tends eggs and fry.
sections.ecology: Its closest lookalike is Apistogramma bitaeniata; the bold dark blotch low on the tail stalk distinguishes A. eremnopyge.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment lists the species as Least Concern, last assessed in 2014. Later Peruvian research notes that narrow-range Apistogramma may be sensitive to forest loss and other habitat change.
